source.title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals

accepted.question_text: Let (A, A) be an arbitrary maximal Banach ideal. Must the principle of A-local reflexivity always hold? Concretely, for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every finite-dimensional subspace F of Y', every operator T in L(E, Y''), and every epsilon > 0, does there always exist an operator S in L(E, Y) such that A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T), the pairing identity <Sx, y'> = <y', Tx> holds for all (x, y') in E x F, and j_Y Sx = Tx for every x in T^{-1}(j_Y(Y))? Equivalently, is there any maximal Banach ideal for which this A-LRP factorization property fails?
accepted.context_brief: A-local reflexivity for maximal Banach ideals

evidence.quote: It seems to be still an open problem whether it is always possible to transfer the norm estimation in the far-reaching classical principle of local reflexivity to the ideal norm A. If this were not the case, we would be very interested in constructing an explicit counterexample. More precisely, we would like to know whether there exists a maximal Banach ideal (A0, A0) which does not satisfy the following factorization property:

We say that the principle of A-local reflexivity (short: A-LRP) is satisfied, if for every T ∈ L(E, Y ′′) there exists an operator S ∈ L(E, Y ) such that (i) A(S) ≤ (1 + ǫ) · A(T); (ii) hSx, y′i = hy′, T xi for all (x, y′) ∈ E × F; (iii) jY Sx = T x for all x ∈ T−1(jY (Y )).
Problem 1.2 Does every maximal Banach ideal satisfy the A-LRP?

accepted.question_text: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two conditions equivalent: first, that (A, A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every operator T in L(E, Y), and every epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and an operator S in L(E, N) with T = J_N^Y S and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T); and second, that (A, A) satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle described in Definition 1.1?

evidence.quote: (B, B) is called right-accessible, if for any two Banach spaces E and Y , dim(E) < ∞, any operator T ∈ L(E, Y ) and any ε > 0 there are a finite dimensional subspace N of Y and S ∈ L(E, N) such that T = JYN S and B(S) ≤ (1 + ε)B(T).
Proposition 1.4 (cf. [13]) If (A, A) is a right-accessible maximal Banach ideal, then the A-LRP holds. We still do not know whether the statement in Proposition 1.4 can be reversed.
Problem 1.5 Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are then the following statements equivalent? (i) (A, A) is right-accessible. (ii) (A, A) satisfies the A-LRP.

accepted.question_text: Let (A_P, A_P) be Pisier's explicitly constructed maximal Banach ideal that is known not to be right-accessible. Does this specific ideal nevertheless satisfy the A_P-local reflexivity principle? That is, does the A-LRP from Definition 1.1 hold when A is specialized to A_P?

evidence.quote: In 1993, Pisier constructed explicitly a maximal Banach ideal (AP , AP ) which is not right-accessible...
Problem 1.6 Does (AP , AP ) satisfy the AP -LRP?

accepted.question_text: Does the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 admit an ideal norm? Equivalently, is the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)** ◦ L2 normed?
accepted.context_brief: Normed product ideal with L2 factor

evidence.quote: Here is a nice application of Theorem 2.3: Put A := (L1 ◦ L∞)∗∗. Due to Grothendieck’s inequality in operator form, it follows that L2 ⊆ A∗ ... Hence, in view of Theorem 2.3, a natural question appears:
Problem 2.4 Is the product ideal (L1 ◦ L∞)∗∗ ◦ L2 normed?
However, we do not know criteria which are sufficient for the existence of an ideal-norm on a given product of quasi-Banach ideals.

accepted.question_text: Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does the product ideal C2* ◦ L∞ have property (I), meaning that for every epsilon > 0 and every finite-rank operator L in C2* ◦ L∞, one can factor L = AB so that A(A) B(B) <= (1 + epsilon) (C2* ◦ L∞)(L) and one of the factors has finite-dimensional range?

evidence.quote: Given ε > 0, any finite rank operator L ∈ A◦B can be factorized as L = AB such that A(A)·B(B) ≤ (1+ε)·A◦B(L) and A respectively B has finite dimensional range. Product ideals A ◦ B of this type are said to have property (I) respectively property (S).
Problem 2.8 Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does C∗2 ◦ L∞ have property (I)?

accepted.question_text: Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal, and let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X0' and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B*(X0, Y0) is not contained in L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ has property (I), does it already follow that the B-LRP is not satisfied, even without assuming that B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible? In other words, can the right-accessibility hypothesis on B ◦ L∞ be removed from this implication?

evidence.quote: Corollary 2.6 Let (B, B) be a maximal Banach ideal. Let X0 and Y0 be Banach spaces such that X′0 and Y0 are of cotype 2 and B∗(X0, Y0) 6⊆ L2(X0, Y0). If B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible and has property (I), then the B-LRP is not satisfied.
Problem 2.9 Can we drop the assumption “ B ◦ L∞ is right-accessible” in Corollary 2.6?
